name: Nate Victor
hero: Nate Victor. Self-taught since 13. No college. 7 ventures started, 5 ended, 2 running. Building until something wins.

timeline.name: MedStrata AI
timeline.text: Founder and CEO. Building the fully autonomous back office for independent pharmacies. 1M+ claims analyzed and $23K+ in identified savings and revenue recovery opportunities.

timeline.name: SDR, Empower Sleep
timeline.text: For 4 months, booked 4 to 10 qualified meetings a day for our account executive. Learned to sell into healthcare.

timeline.name: InsureFlow AI
timeline.text: Claude brought coding back for me. Built an AI operating system for life insurance agents to compete with GoHighLevel. Too ambitious for the wrong audience, and the co-founder relationship ended badly.

timeline.name: Smart Frost Film
timeline.text: Resold smart film that switches glass from clear to frosted with a remote. Sold 3 customers. The supplier never delivered, and no one else could match the price. Shut it down to focus on building a tech company.

timeline.name: Life insurance agent and team lead
timeline.text: Got licensed, built a team of 6 agents, and ran our own Facebook ads system. Best month: over $30,000. Then chargebacks hit, and it fell apart.

timeline.name: Graduated high school
timeline.text: Skipped college. Everything since, I taught myself.

timeline.name: Appointment setter, life insurance
timeline.text: Booked qualified appointments for a life insurance agent at $100 each.

timeline.name: Real estate marketing agency
timeline.text: A few older friends were real estate agents who couldn't get Facebook ads to bring in leads. I figured it out, then sold them ads and leads. Grew to 12 agent clients and $15K MRR at peak. Built their GoHighLevel CRMs and Zapier automations.

timeline.name: Oasis VRX
timeline.text: First job, at a VR arcade.

timeline.name: E-commerce
timeline.text: Built and ran online stores. Most lost to competition.

timeline.name: Prime High School Fantasy Sports
timeline.text: At 13, taught myself JavaScript and spent 8 months building a fantasy sports and betting app for my friends and their dads. It worked. Apple rejected it. Betting apps have to come from licensed companies, and I was a 13-year-old with a laptop.

lessons: Rules can kill a product that works. I learned that at 13.
Revenue isn't real until the chargebacks clear.
In crowded markets, competition kills you before customers do.
Never sell what you can't deliver.
Every flop made the next build faster.
closing: Next: make MedStrata the back office every independent pharmacy runs on.
